eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent rainfall and cloud cover expected on August 16 are the main drivers keeping trader-implied odds highest for a daily maximum of 26°C in Busan.**

Korea Meteorological Administration short-range forecasts project a minimum near 24°C and maximum of 30°C under continued rain (60-70% probability), with some models and sites like timeanddate.com indicating highs closer to 26°C (79°F) amid overcast conditions. This follows an intense late-July heatwave that produced a record 38.8°C in the Busan area, but recent heavy rain across southern South Korea is cooling the region and suppressing typical August daytime heating.

Seasonal averages for Busan highs hover around 29–30°C, yet the current pattern of widespread precipitation and reduced solar radiation favors lower maxima. Traders appear to be weighting these near-term atmospheric conditions more heavily than climatology, resulting in the 64% implied probability on 26°C, modest support for 27–28°C, and negligible odds on extremes above 29°C or below 25°C. Updated model runs and official KMA briefings ahead of resolution will be the key variables to watch.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Wellington Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 17 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Wellington Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/nz/wellington/NZWN.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
